## 4. Mutation operations

All successes below are `Receipt<...>`. `201` responses include `Location` naming
the current learner's `/api/student?learnerId=…&runId=…&sessionId=…`. All `202`
responses include the same `Location` plus `Retry-After: 1`. `202` means the job
has been admitted and assigned a job ID, not that a provider result succeeded.
Poll StudentSnapshot to observe its terminal or review state. The server never
holds the HTTP response open until a provider finishes. The transient
`ready_for_assessment` state is observable; assessment always requires its own
explicit operation.

### Submit immutable work

`POST /api/attempts` receives:

```text
E + {learnerId, assignmentId, attemptId, expectedAssignmentRevision,
     expectedTargetCorrectionRevision, imagePngBase64: string | null,
     strokes: Stroke[], writtenWorking: string,
     explanationMode: "spoken" | "written", initialText: string | null}
```

`imagePngBase64` is canonical padded base64 without a data-URL prefix, whitespace,
or URL-safe alphabet. PNG admission and the separate raster bound follow the
[media contract](media_contract.md). Require an admitted image or nonempty
trimmed `writtenWorking`; strokes alone are not submitted work. No image requires
`strokes: []`; an image can have no strokes. Total points are bounded across all
strokes. `writtenWorking` is at most 4,000 code points and counts toward retained
text history. Written mode requires nonempty `initialText` at most 4,000 code
points; spoken mode requires `initialText: null`.

Only the current assignment accepts new work. Reject an attemptId already used
under a different idempotency key with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Admission atomically
allocates its next workVersion, evidenceVersion 1, and initial turnId; makes it
the assignment's active attempt; increments assignmentRevision; and supersedes
any pending job for the previous attempt. Retain earlier work/history. Check all
capacity/PNG/text bounds before doing any of this. No provider call starts.

Return `201 Receipt<AttemptResult>` with `turnId` initial turn, `jobId: null`, and
state `awaiting_audio` (spoken) or `ready_for_assessment` (written). The initial
written turn is already confirmed. A submission's new expected assignment
revision is returned in `assignmentRevision`.

### Upload one completed audio turn

`POST /api/attempts/:id/audio?turnId=UUID` has binary bytes as its entire body.
Require these headers instead of JSON:

```text
Content-Type: audio/webm;codecs=opus | audio/webm | audio/mp4 | audio/wav
X-Run-Id, X-Session-Id, X-Idempotency-Key,
X-Learner-Id, X-Assignment-Id, X-Expected-Assignment-Revision,
X-Expected-Evidence-Version, X-Expected-Target-Correction-Revision
```

Header revision values are canonical nonnegative base-10 strings. Accept case
insensitive MIME tokens/parameter ordering; normalize MIME for fingerprinting.
Reject unsupported parameters/codecs, empty bodies, or a container signature that
does not match the declared type. This is bounded format admission, not a claim
to verify duration or speech meaning. A turn must be the active unfilled spoken
turn in `awaiting_audio`. Admission reserves one of two provider slots, records
the job, and enters `transcribing`. Return `202 Receipt<AttemptResult>` with the
audio turnId and jobId. The byte buffer is transient and released on every
completion, rejection, abort, failure, timeout, and shutdown path.

A successful transcription stores bounded recognized text, increments
evidenceVersion, and enters `awaiting_transcript_review`. It does not assess.
An empty/unusable or over-limit transcription fails visibly without inventing
text; the attempt enters `failed`. A transcription job timeout/failure appears
in Attempt `error`; the already returned 202 is not rewritten to an HTTP error.

### Confirm text and start assessment

`POST /api/attempts/:id/assessment` receives:

```text
AE + {confirmedTurns: [{turnId: UUID, text: string}]}
```

Supply exactly all current turns, once each and in their stored order; each text
is nonempty and at most 4,000 code points. No audio-pending/transcribing turn can
be confirmed. Initial written text or previous confirmed text can be sent
unchanged. Preserve recognized/original text and every edit. An actual edit or
new confirmation increments evidenceVersion once for this whole operation, not
once per turn. Enforce the 12,000 assembled-text, 16-turn, 16-evidence-version,
and 64 KiB UTF-8 retained-history limits before commitment. Limits are separate;
an unchanged confirmation consumes neither a version nor a turn.

The attempt's assignment must still be the learner's current assignment.
Historical evidence remains visible; correct a historical judgment through
teacher retraction rather than learner reassessment. Allowed from
`ready_for_assessment`, `awaiting_transcript_review`,
`needs_clarification`, or a current `accepted`/`awaiting_readback` attempt when its
confirmed text is being corrected. In the latter cases require an actual text
edit; unchanged accepted work cannot be repeatedly assessed. A recognition edit
of already-confirmed text invalidates the old candidate and that attempt's
judgments based on replaced evidence, as specified by the learning contract;
it increments
the target correctionRevision if a committed judgment was invalidated, and
replays that target before starting the new job. Slot/bounds validation precedes
the whole correction; a busy rejection cannot invalidate old evidence.

Reserve a provider slot and return `202 Receipt<AttemptResult>` with `turnId:
null`, new/current evidenceVersion, new/current targetCorrectionRevision, and
assessment jobId. On validated success: an image goes to `awaiting_readback`;
text-only evidence commits synchronously within the job completion and enters
`accepted` or `needs_clarification` according to its validated observations.
An uncertainty/conflict is a learning outcome, not a provider failure. A malformed
or ungrounded result enters `failed` with its safe error and commits no judgment.

### Confirm the neutral image readback

`POST /api/attempts/:id/readback` receives:

```text
AE + {candidateId: UUID, matches: boolean}
```

Only the current attempt's `awaiting_readback` candidate can be addressed. `matches: true`
confirms the image source, then commits the candidate through learning validation
exactly once. A validated usable judgment enters `accepted`; uncertainty/conflict
enters `needs_clarification`, preserving earlier supported findings. `matches:
false` records a mismatch, invalidates that uncommitted candidate, increments
evidenceVersion once, and enters `needs_clarification`. It commits no disputed
math judgment and shows the authored recognition prompt. The next clarification
can describe the marks; editing the board instead requires a new attempt. No
provider starts here. Return `200 Receipt<AttemptResult>`, `turnId/jobId: null`.

### Add a clarification turn

`POST /api/attempts/:id/clarifications` receives exactly one union branch:

```text
AE + {mode: "written", text: string}
AE + {mode: "spoken"}
```

The spoken branch has no `text` key. A written clarification is nonempty and at
most 4,000 code points. Allow this in `needs_clarification`, or in `accepted`
after the most recent `/next` applied a current-assignment neutral prompt or
teaching action that requests another explanation. No pending turn/job may
exist. Append a new turnId, preserve previous turns/work, and increment
evidenceVersion once. Appending reasoning does not invalidate a prior committed
judgment or increment correctionRevision: its assessment adds a chronological
judgment and updates only the Attempt's latest acceptedJudgmentId pointer.
Earlier difficulty remains valid history and clears only through the learning
rules' fresh independent evidence. Editing an already-confirmed source or an
explicit correction can invalidate earlier support. Return
`201 Receipt<AttemptResult>` with
the new turnId and `jobId: null`. Written mode enters `ready_for_assessment` and
requires `/assessment` with all turns; spoken mode enters `awaiting_audio`, then
requires audio, transcript review, and `/assessment` in that order. Clarification
never changes assistance automatically; an authored teaching/warmup action has
already marked assistance before being displayed.

### Cancel processing

`POST /api/attempts/:id/cancel` receives `AE`, with no extra keys. From any state
other than `accepted` or already `cancelled`, cancel its active work, invalidate
its commit token, abort its jobs, stop processing, and release transient audio.
No admitted PNG/history or committed older judgment is deleted. An accepted
attempt has no pending processing to cancel and returns `INVALID_TRANSITION`.
An already-cancelled attempt with current context returns 200 with its current
projection, including under a new key; it has no additional side effects. Return
`200 Receipt<AttemptResult>` with `turnId/jobId: null` and state `cancelled`.
Do not increment evidenceVersion or target correctionRevision for cancellation.
The next submission is a new attempt. Failed/cancelled attempts cannot resume.

### Apply help or issue the next assignment

`POST /api/learners/:id/next` receives:

```text
E + {learnerId, assignmentId, expectedAssignmentRevision,
     expectedTargetCorrectionRevision, actionId}
```

Require the route/body learner, current assignment identity, and one current
`allowedActions` actionId. No processing/readback/transcript confirmation may be
pending. The learning contract supplies the finite catalog and complete decision
table. The server returns the same action it accepted; a scheduler-dependent
action must already be the action offered by the preceding snapshot.

* `current_assignment`: record the action event, increment assignmentRevision,
  record assistance before returning teaching/warmup material when applicable,
  and return the same assignmentId/problem/workVersion. Neutral prompts do not
  consume problems or clear findings.
* `new_assignment`: complete the old assignment if the learning rules permit,
  allocate a new assignmentId/revision 0 and the next authored problem, and
  consume a pool entry only as specified by the scheduler. No attempt or evidence
  is pre-created. Independent eligibility is server-owned.
* `session_status`: record `request-teacher-review` or `finish-session`, keep the
  last assignment/history, and set the corresponding sessionStatus. It never
  creates a repeated problem merely to fill a pool gap.

Return `200 Receipt<{performedAction: PerformedAction,
assignment: Assignment | null, student: StudentSnapshot}>`. First assignment
creation happens with session initialization, not by calling `/next` on null.

### Retract unsupported judgments

`POST /api/findings/:id/retractions` receives:

```text
E + {learnerId, targetId, expectedFindingRevision,
     expectedTargetCorrectionRevision, judgmentIds: UUID[], reason: string}
```

Require a nonempty unique list (at most 128) of currently valid judgments in
that exact finding/learner/target history and a trimmed reason of 1–500 code
points. Reject mixed targets, unknown judgments, or already invalid judgments
without partial retraction. Mark the selected judgments invalid, append one
Correction, increment that target correctionRevision once, invalidate only its
pending jobs, replay it chronologically, and produce one atomic new snapshot.
Retain issued assignments, consumed pools, original evidence, and correction
history; follow the learning contract's corrected obligations for future issue.
Restore current attempts whose jobs were invalidated to ready_for_assessment,
awaiting_transcript_review, or awaiting_audio according to their retained turns,
as specified by learning. Retraction of the current committed judgment with no
active job enters needs_clarification. Historical attempts remain read-only.
Return `200 Receipt<{findingId, correctionId, findingRevision,
targetCorrectionRevision, teacher: TeacherSnapshot}>`. Teacher and poll responses
use the same monotonic session revision rule.

### Reset the current session

`POST /api/reset` receives `E + {expectedSessionRevision}`. Require the current
session-wide revision. Reset is available even at capacity or during processing.
Atomically invalidate/cancel all jobs, release all admitted images and transient
audio, clear previous attempts/judgments/help/corrections/idempotency records,
allocate a new sessionId (same runId), reset revision to zero, recreate the fixed
roster/stable target findings and initial addition assignments, and return
`200 Receipt<{context: Context, teacher: TeacherSnapshot}>` in the **new**
context. This response has `replayed: false`; a retry of the old-session request
returns `CONTEXT_CHANGED` with the new context identities. There is no implicit
reset in startup seeding, a read, a provider failure, or a browser refresh.

## 5. Finite safe error catalog

Every API error body is exactly:

```text
{error: {code: ErrorCode, message: catalog string, retryable: boolean},
 runId: UUID, sessionId: UUID}
```

Those IDs identify the server's current context, including a context mismatch.
No details/raw exception/provider body is added. Failed jobs use the same inner
`{code,message,retryable}` as Attempt `error`. The HTTP column below applies when
the failure can be known before a response; after 202 it is the snapshot error
classification. `retryable` means a later user-authorized fresh operation can
succeed under the stated condition; there are no automatic paid retries.

| Code | HTTP | Message (exact) | Retryable / recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | 400 | `Check the submitted fields.` | false; correct body/query/headers, including invalid JSON or IDs |
| `RESOURCE_MISMATCH` | 400 | `The submitted work does not match this request.` | false; correct route/body ownership |
| `INVALID_PNG` | 400 | `The drawing file is damaged or invalid.` | false; re-export admitted PNG |
| `INVALID_AUDIO` | 400 | `The recording file is empty or invalid.` | false; record again or use writing |
| `ORIGIN_REJECTED` | 403 | `Open the app from its local address.` | false; correct Host/Origin |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `This item is not available in the current session.` | false; refresh current state |
| `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `This address is not available.` | false; correct route |
| `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | 405 | `This action is not available at this address.` | false; response also has `Allow` with the supported verb(s) |
| `CONTEXT_CHANGED` | 409 | `The demo session changed. Refresh to continue.` | false; fetch context, discard old actions |
| `REVISION_CONFLICT` | 409 | `This work changed. Refresh before continuing.` | false; fetch current snapshot, intentionally retry under a new key |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` | 409 | `This request identity was already used for different content.` | false; correct accidental key reuse |
| `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` | 409 | `This work identity was already submitted.` | false; recover its accepted result or use a new attemptId |
| `INVALID_TRANSITION` | 409 | `Complete the current step before this action.` | false; refresh and follow allowed actions |
| `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` | 409 | `Choose an action offered for the current work.` | false; refresh allowedActions |
| `REQUEST_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | `This submission is too large.` | false; reduce JSON/audio/retained turn-history input |
| `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | `The drawing exceeds the allowed size.` | false; re-export within file/raster/dimension bounds |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA` | 415 | `Use a supported recording or JSON format.` | false; negotiate recording format or use writing |
| `UNSUPPORTED_PNG` | 415 | `Use a supported PNG drawing format.` | false; re-export admitted PNG subset |
| `PROCESSING_BUSY` | 429 | `Two explanations are processing. Try again shortly.` | true; no admission; `Retry-After: 1` |
| `SESSION_CAPACITY` | 429 | `This demo is full. Reset or restart to add work.` | false; prior evidence remains; reset/restart is explicit |
| `INTERPRETATION_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | `The explanation could not be processed. Try new work or use writing.` | true; new attempt or non-speech route; no finding |
| `INTERPRETATION_INVALID` | 502 | `The returned interpretation could not be verified. Try new work or use writing.` | true; malformed schema, ungrounded source, invalid action or impossible provider claims; no finding |
| `FIXTURE_UNMATCHED` | 502 | `This input has no prepared example. Use the documented example or switch modes.` | false; fixture mode only; never fall back to live |
| `INTERPRETATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | `Processing took too long. Try new work or use writing.` | true; new attempt; no finding |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | `The app could not complete this action.` | false; preserve prior snapshot; operator may restart |

Unknown provider errors map to `INTERPRETATION_UNAVAILABLE`; syntax/schema/source
failures map to `INTERPRETATION_INVALID`; AbortError from a known cancellation is
not a failed learning result. Explicit cancellation is a successful 200 response,
not an error. Unsupported fixture controls/configuration fail server startup;
they are not new public API errors.

Validation precedence is Host/Origin and method/route, bounded parse/media shape,
current context, idempotency replay/conflict, resource ownership, expected
revisions, state/action eligibility, per-attempt and session bounds, provider
slot, then atomic admission. PNG errors are produced by PNG admission before
state mutation. Exceeding HTTP body byte caps can terminate input consumption;
the server still returns the safe 413 when the connection permits. No failed
validation consumes a pool slot, invalidates a judgment, or changes a count.

## 6. Browser reconciliation

Use `cache: "no-store"` for API reads and fetch exact work URLs without browser
storage. After a mutation replace local state only with the same-context
snapshot whose revision is at least the displayed revision. Reject older
snapshot responses, including a poll that arrives after a correction. A new
run/session disposes the old timer, in-flight fetch, capture, and pending actions,
then loads the new context rather than comparing revisions across sessions.
Keep last-known teacher data visibly stale on errors; never replace it with
zeros. Poll immediately, then 1,000 ms after settlement, with one request/timer
and a 5,000 ms request timeout. Student polling runs only during processing;
operation responses and explicit refresh handle the other states.

# Injected interpretation, prepared examples, and class seed — DR-04

This resolution freezes the seam used by the live adapter, fixture adapter,
server tests, browser tests, and seeder. It adds no application, network call,
credential access, framework, queue, or storage. Public operations and projections
are exactly the [HTTP contract](api_contract.md); learning outcomes follow the
[learning contract](learning_contract.md). Fixture use remains visibly labelled
and does not satisfy the live multimodal gate.

## 1. Application and adapter injection

`server.mjs` exports this single constructor:

```text
createApp({config, lesson, adapter,
           now = () => new Date(), newId = crypto.randomUUID})
  -> {server: node:http.Server, close: () => Promise<void>}
```

`config`, parsed by `src/config.mjs`, and the complete validated
`content/demo-lesson.json` object are required. `adapter` is required; the
executable entry point constructs the selected live or fixture adapter before
calling `createApp`. Tests supply the same interface. There is no hidden default
adapter or fallback from live to fixture. `now()` returns a valid Date; `newId()`
returns a fresh canonical UUID. Those two synchronous seams permit deterministic
IDs/time in tests without an alternate state store. The constructor validates
configuration/content and creates fresh process-memory state and a new runId;
it creates the server without listening. Call Node's `server.listen` on the
selected loopback host/port. `close()` is repeatable, invalidates all jobs,
aborts/release transient resources, releases admitted media/state, and closes a
listening server. The returned object exposes no mutable records or fixture
selector; tests verify behavior through HTTP.

Both adapters implement exactly:

```text
adapter.transcribe(input: TranscribeInput) -> Promise<{text: string}>
adapter.assess(input: AssessInput) -> Promise<Candidate>
adapter.cancel({jobId: UUID, reason: CancelReason}) -> Promise<void>

CancelReason = "superseded" | "correction" | "cancelled" | "reset" |
               "shutdown" | "timeout"
JobContext = {jobId, runId, sessionId, learnerId, assignmentId,
              assignmentRevision, targetId, attemptId, workVersion,
              evidenceVersion, correctionRevision}
FrozenWork = {image: {bytes: Uint8Array, sha256: lowercaseHex64,
                     width: integer, height: integer} | null,
              imageSourceId: string | null, strokes: Stroke[],
              writtenWorking: string}
AdapterProblem = {problemId, targetId, operation: "add" | "subtract",
                  left: integer, right: integer, prompt: string,
                  purpose: "practice" | "check" | "review",
                  assisted: boolean}
TranscribeInput = {job: JobContext, problem: AdapterProblem, work: FrozenWork,
                   turn: {turnId, index: integer, source: "transcription"},
                   audio: {bytes: Uint8Array, mimeType: string},
                   signal: AbortSignal}
ConfirmedTurn = {turnId, source: "transcription" | "written", text: string}
AssessInput = {job: JobContext, problem: AdapterProblem, work: FrozenWork,
               turns: ConfirmedTurn[], criteria: Criteria,
               allowedActionIds: string[], signal: AbortSignal}
Criteria = {criterionId: "conserve-value-addition" | "conserve-value-subtraction",
            expectedAnswer: integer, before: {tens: integer, ones: integer},
            conservedAfter: {tens: integer, ones: integer},
            difficultyCode: "addition-omitted-ten" | "subtraction-value-changed"}
```

All input fields are required, including nullable image fields. `index` is the
zero-based turn position. An image source ID is exactly
`attemptId + ":work:" + workVersion`; no image means both image fields are null.
Adapter image bytes are the immutable normalized admitted PNG defined in the
[media contract](media_contract.md), not a second copy of client metadata.
For addition, Criteria `before` is the combined original tens/ones and
`conservedAfter` is the normalized exchange; for subtraction they describe the
minuend before/after the one-ten exchange. Compute every quantity/answer from
authored operands, never from provider advice. `allowedActionIds` is the complete
finite authored action catalog, not the learner's currently eligible next actions
and not a requested diagnosis. A known but inapplicable proposed action is ignored
by the learning controller, which derives the eligible action from the validated
evidence and scheduler; an unknown action ID fails validation. Neither input contains teacher counts,
a desired category, a fixture ID, or a claimed finding transition.

The server retains ownership of input buffers and snapshots; adapters must not
mutate them, persist them, log them, or retain their references after settlement.
An adapter holds only its current cancellation handles. Audio is released by the
server's `finally` path as well as adapter-local cleanup. `cancel` aborts its
named job if present and is a no-op if already settled/unknown. It is safe to
repeat. The AbortSignal is the immediate propagation path; the explicit method
also lets the server release adapter-owned resources. Cancellation never
changes learning state itself. Late settlement is always checked against
JobContext and the server's commit token before any state change.

Adapter rejection is an `Error` with `name: "InterpretationError"` and a finite
`code`: `unavailable`, `invalid`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, or `fixture_unmatched`.
Use the HTTP catalog's corresponding safe error; raw error strings are never
returned or logged with user media. A known abort leaves the already selected
cancelled/superseded state, rather than adding a failure. The server owns the
45-second deadline and two-call limit for both adapters. No adapter performs
automatic retries. A fixture may simulate a delayed result that ignores abort
only through the startup test controls below, to prove the server rejects it.

The live implementation keeps the approved models/endpoints, structured output,
bounded response, and project-only credential behavior from `design_draft.md`.
Its transcription provider call receives audio only; the extra local problem/work
fields exist so the fixture implementation can match the same server-owned
request context. Assessment sends frozen work, confirmed turns, authored operands,
the symbolic target rubric, and allowed authored action IDs. Criteria's computed
expectedAnswer/before/conservedAfter remain local validation inputs for every
mode and never enter the outbound provider prompt or probe request. The provider
is not handed a case-specific answer key or expected classification.
The transport injection for unit-testing the live
adapter remains internal to `src/assessment-adapter.mjs`; it does not add an API.

## 2. Assessment result and common validation

`Candidate` has exactly these required fields, with no additional properties:

```text
{category: CandidateCategory, observedAnswer: safe integer | null,
 exchangeEvidence: "supported" | "contradicted" | "not_established" | "unclear",
 recognitionStatus: "usable" | "clarify" | "conflict",
 sourceEvidence: SourceEvidence[], exchangeQuantities: Quantities | null,
 neutralReadback: string, reasoningSummary: string, teachingMoveId: string}

CandidateCategory = "supported_exchange" | "addition_omitted_ten" |
 "subtraction_value_changed" | "procedure_without_exchange_explanation" |
 "correct_answer_without_reasoning" | "valid_alternative_strategy" |
 "computation_error" | "needs_clarification"
SourceEvidence = {sourceKind: "turn" | "image", sourceId: string,
                  quote: string | null, description: string}
Quantities = {before: {tens: integer 0..999, ones: integer 0..999},
              after: {tens: integer 0..999, ones: integer 0..999}}
```

`sourceEvidence` has at most ten entries. A turn entry requires an existing
confirmed turnId and a nonempty exact substring quote from that turn. An image
entry requires the current imageSourceId, `quote: null`, and nonempty description;
it cannot cite an absent image or a previous attempt. Quotes/descriptions are
at most 500 code points each; reasoningSummary at most 500 and neutralReadback
at most 1,200. A non-clarification category requires usable supporting source
entries. An unrecognizable `needs_clarification` can have no source entries.
Text-only input requires `neutralReadback: ""` and no image source entry. For an
image, neutralReadback describes only submitted marks/quantities; it must not
include an expected solution, correctness verdict, teaching step, or a worked
correction. The student sees it before any candidate math feedback.

Every adapter result passes one shared server path: strict schema and size;
current source identity and exact quotes; independently computed authored answer;
observed quantities and conservation/error predicates; cross-modal consistency;
full action-catalog membership followed by controller selection from the authored
table; recognition readback when an image exists;
then learning reduction. Fixture mode has no bypass flag. The adapter proposes
neither `answerCorrect`, `canClearFinding`, counts, independence, nor mastery.
Only the server derives those values. Source/schema failure is
`INTERPRETATION_INVALID`; actual wrong learner numbers remain admissible grounded
evidence. Unclear/conflicting content is `needs_clarification`, with no disputed
new difficulty/clearing, rather than an invented error code.

The shared validation entry points belong in the selected `src/learning.mjs`
and the server's processing path. The live adapter validates its provider
boundary too, but callers still run common validation after any injected result.
The fixture adapter returns fresh copies of provider-shaped observations, never
prebuilt Attempt/Judgment/Finding objects or teacher snapshots.

## 3. Server-owned fixture matching

`test/fixtures/regrouping-cases.json` is the one authored text/observation
catalog used by the fixture adapter, audio probe, seed script, and browser tests.
It contains the six canonical `audio-*` cases from the
[verification contract](verification_contract.md), the seed rows below, and
image/readback/invalid-output cases needed by the browser/server checks. Case
names are private test/catalog identifiers; none is a mutation field.

`test/fixture-adapter.mjs` exports
`createFixtureAdapter({catalog, controls: FixtureControl[]})`. The executable
uses it only when `ASSESSMENT_MODE=fixture` was explicitly selected. Live mode
must reject attempts to load fixture catalogs/controls and must never instantiate
the fixture adapter. Both views display “Prepared examples” whenever Context
processingMode is fixture; errors do not silently change modes.

The JSON catalog has exactly `{version: 1, cases: FixtureCase[]}`. Each case has
exactly the following required keys:

```text
FixtureCase = {caseId: string, problemId: string,
               purpose: "practice" | "check" | "review", assisted: boolean,
               writtenWorking: string, strokes: Stroke[],
               imagePngBase64: string | null,
               turns: FixtureTurn[], candidate: CandidateTemplate}
FixtureTurn = {source: "written" | "transcription", text: string,
               audioCaseId: string | null, browserAudioClasses: string[]}
```

CandidateTemplate is exactly Candidate with sourceId placeholders described
below. Written turns require audioCaseId null and browserAudioClasses empty;
spoken turns reference one of the six canonical audio case IDs and explicitly
allow `browser-webm-opus` and/or `browser-mp4`. Audio hashes are computed from the
generated canonical WAVs, not invented or copied from removed old probe files.
`test/fixture-adapter.mjs` also exports `prepareFixtureCatalog({catalog,
canonicalWavs})` and `makeFixturePng({width,height,rgba})`: the former validates
closed catalog rows and builds the private indexes, the latter produces bounded
synthetic RGBA PNG bytes with built-in Buffer, `node:zlib.deflateSync`, and
`node:zlib.crc32`, then passes them through `src/png.mjs` admission. These are
test helpers within the existing file allowlist, not runtime dependencies.
`canonicalWavs` is a map from audioCaseId to Uint8Array WAV bytes and can be
empty for written/browser-only fixture operation. The helper returns private
PreparedCatalog indexes; `createFixtureAdapter` receives that result as its
`catalog` argument. Exact-WAV matching is available only for the supplied map
entries; browser class matching still uses the registered canonical text row.
All canonical audio rows use text-only work `Synthetic audio probe. <problemId>.`,
empty strokes, practice purpose, no assistance, and the exact canonical spoken
text; probe-created IDs are substituted at call time. Seed rows use section 5.

The catalog indexes the actual input, not a requested outcome:

```text
WorkKey = SHA256(canonicalJSON({problemId, writtenWorking, strokes,
                               normalizedImageSha256: string | null}))
AssessmentKey = SHA256(canonicalJSON({workKey, purpose, assisted,
                                     confirmedTexts: string[]}))
TranscriptionKey = {workKey, turnIndex, audioClass}
audioClass = "canonical-wav:<sha256>" | "browser-webm-opus" | "browser-mp4"
```

Use canonical JSON object-key order as written, arrays in their original order,
UTF-8, and exact strings (no trimming/case normalization of evidence). IDs,
timestamps, revisions, and learner identity are excluded from keys; they are
bound by JobContext instead. Canonical WAV files require exact byte SHA-256.
Browser capture uses the negotiated container class because MediaRecorder
container bytes are not reproducible. It still requires matching frozen work,
turn ordinal, supported nonempty media, and the preselected fake-microphone
recipe. The simulated transcript is explicit; fixture tests do not establish
recognition of arbitrary audio. Assessment requires the subsequently confirmed
text to match, so a fixture cannot impose a finding on different words.

Each unique key has exactly one catalog row; duplicate ambiguous keys fail
startup. The server/adapter chooses it after admission. No `fixtureCaseId`,
category, transcript override, delay, or malformed-output switch is accepted in
public JSON, headers, query parameters, browser storage, or live configuration.
Human fixture rehearsal uses the published authored work and exact words;
typing different content can deliberately exercise unmatched handling. A
prepared example can be selected locally in a test before submitting its real
work; that local name is never sent to the application API.

Template source placeholders `$turn[0]`, `$turn[1]`, and `$image` are replaced only
with the actual request source IDs. Templates contain exact literal quotes from
their expected confirmed text; substitution never changes quotes, quantities,
or categories. If the input has an image, its registered normalized PNG hash
must match the actual drawing. Browser image cases use fixed catalogued strokes
and a deterministic white-board PNG built by `makeFixturePng`. Their test setup
admits those exact bytes through POST attempts, then opens/refreshes the normal
student view to exercise audio, transcript, image readback, and feedback controls.
It adds no image-import/fixture-selection feature to the product.
A separate drawing/export browser test uses actual pointer events and validates
the resulting admitted PNG/strokes without pretending an uncatalogued picture
was interpreted. Real freehand interpretation is verified by the live gate.

The input request's idempotency fingerprint uses the original admitted request
bytes; fixture work matching uses the media contract's normalized image SHA.
Ancillary-chunk stripping can therefore produce the same fixture WorkKey for
two different raw submissions without making them idempotent retries.

An unmatched transcribe/assess key rejects with `fixture_unmatched`. After 202,
the attempt becomes `failed` with `FIXTURE_UNMATCHED`, releasing audio/provider
slots and retaining the drawing/history. It never calls live services, chooses
a nearby case, guesses a category, or manufactures a normal success. All fixture
catalogs and helpers are credential-free and make no external requests.

## 4. Delay, malformed-result, and browser audio controls

Fixture controls are constructor-only test data, separate from the content
catalog. Each control has exactly:

```text
{operation: "transcribe" | "assess", matchKey: string,
 occurrence: positive integer, delayMs: integer 0..60000,
 ignoresAbort: boolean,
 result: "normal" | "malformed_schema" | "ungrounded_quote" |
         "unsupported_action" | "unavailable"}
```

`matchKey` names a known private catalog key, `occurrence` counts matching calls
within that one adapter instance, and no duplicate control can target the same
call. Unspecified calls use zero delay, respect abort, and return normal data.
`malformed_schema` returns one deliberately invalid shape, `ungrounded_quote`
changes a quote to absent text, `unsupported_action` returns an unlisted action,
and `unavailable` throws the classified unavailable error. Non-normal
transcription controls allow only malformed_schema or unavailable; quote/action
controls are assessment-only. The three invalid assessment variants must fail
through the common validator as `INTERPRETATION_INVALID`, not through a fixture
shortcut. Delay beyond 45 seconds proves the real timeout path. The optional
ignoresAbort control proves that a late result cannot overwrite a correction,
replacement, reset, or cancellation. Controls are never populated by HTTP.

Browser spoken cases prepare the specified synthetic WAV before launching their
own Chromium context/process, using the credential-free
`prepareSyntheticAudio()` helper exported by `scripts/live-probe.mjs` and the
exact tools/voice/format in the verification contract. Launch Chromium with
`--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream`, `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and
`--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture=<absolute-wav-path>`. Grant microphone
permission only to the loopback origin. Start and stop through the real learner
recording controls, wait at least the generated WAV duration before Stop, upload
the actual negotiated MediaRecorder output, inspect the fixture transcript, and
confirm/edit it through the real review screen. Use one generated WAV per fresh
context; never the user's microphone. The file must remain until capture ends;
cleanup closes contexts/tracks and removes the private temporary directory in a
finally path. Missing synthesis prerequisites fail before browser launch and
never trigger live/provider calls. Written browser cases need no fake microphone.

Browser tests cover both confirmation and correction, matching/mismatching image
readback, supported and uncertain learning outcomes, refresh, one-second teacher
polling, cancellation/reset with an ignoring-abort delayed job, and malformed
response display. They assert labelled fixture processing. None can be reported

# PNG admission and bounded media contract

Normative resolution of DR-05 and its overlapping size-clarity finding. This
keeps the approved Node 24 built-ins-only runtime. It is a restricted drawing
transport contract, not a general-purpose image decoder or file-upload service.

## Interface and byte units

Create `src/png.mjs` with `admitDrawing(imagePngBase64)`. It returns
`{pngBytes, width, height, colorType, byteLength, sha256}` or a safe typed error.
The input is canonical padded base64 without a data-URL prefix or whitespace.
Decode once and require its base64 round trip to equal the input.

The **1 MiB limit means at most 1,048,576 PNG file bytes after base64 decoding**.
It does not limit the decompressed raster to 1 MiB. Enforce the limit on both
input and admitted PNG bytes. Dimensions are positive and no greater than
1024 × 768. The current-run image budget counts admitted PNG file bytes once per
immutable work version, not temporary raster buffers or duplicate references.

## Admitted subset and algorithm

Use Buffer operations, `node:crypto` for the admitted-image hash, and
`node:zlib.crc32` / `inflateSync`. No runtime image package is introduced.

1. Validate the eight signature bytes `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`.
2. Walk at most 1,024 chunks with bounded length/type/data/CRC reads. Require
   alphabetic four-byte chunk names with the reserved third letter uppercase.
   Verify every CRC over the chunk type and data, using unsigned `crc32`.
3. Require one first `IHDR` of length 13. Admit only bit depth 8, color type 2
   (RGB) or 6 (RGBA), compression/filter method 0, and interlace method 0.
4. Require at least one contiguous `IDAT` sequence and one empty final `IEND`.
   Reject missing/duplicate/misordered required chunks and bytes after `IEND`.
   The only admitted critical chunk types are `IHDR`, `IDAT`, and `IEND`; reject
   every other critical type, including optional `PLTE`, as unsupported. Reject
   animation chunks `acTL`, `fcTL`, and `fdAT`.
5. Other ancillary chunks are CRC-checked but not interpreted or decompressed.
   Strip them from the admitted image. Retain only the original `IHDR`, contiguous
   `IDAT` chunks, and `IEND`, so ignored metadata cannot affect later rendering.
   The accepted drawing preserves its image data; metadata is not archived.
6. For channels `c = 3` or `4`, compute `stride = 1 + width * c` and
   `expected = height * stride`. Concatenate the bounded IDAT data and call
   `inflateSync(data, {maxOutputLength: expected, info: true})`.
7. Require exact output length `expected`, full compressed-input consumption
   (`engine.bytesWritten === data.length`), and a filter byte in 0–4 at the start
   of every row. Any inflate/checksum/truncation/overflow failure rejects the input.
   Pixel reconstruction is unnecessary for this admission check: all byte values
   under those supported row filters are defined. Never inspect text as math here.
8. Release the temporary inflated buffer. Hash/store the admitted PNG, return its
   metadata, and use that same immutable PNG for provider input and teacher review.

The largest temporary filtered raster is 3,146,496 bytes for the full RGBA board.
Its dimension-derived bound is separate from the compressed-file and retained
image-budget limits. Browser export must produce this subset; the first browser
gate verifies actual Chromium canvas export. An unsupported exporter offers the
written route and does not silently weaken admission or change the image policy.

## Errors and checks

| Condition | HTTP/code | State effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base64, signature, chunk, CRC, deflate, row-length/filter, or trailing-data failure | `400 INVALID_PNG` | Reject before image admission/provider work; retain prior evidence |
| A readable header requests unsupported bit depth/color/interlace, animation, `PLTE`, or another critical extension | `415 UNSUPPORTED_PNG` | Offer the supported browser export or written route |
| File bytes or dimensions exceed bounds | `413 IMAGE_TOO_LARGE` | Reject atomically without consuming image budget |

Create `test/png.test.mjs`. Construct tiny valid RGB/RGBA fixtures with built-ins
and test each legal row filter, split consecutive IDAT, metadata stripping,
canonical base64, and the exact dimension/file-byte boundaries. Negative cases
cover missing/duplicate/misordered chunks, truncation, bad CRC, unknown critical
and animation chunks, unsupported headers, bad deflate/adler data, wrong row
length/filter, excessive inflation, concatenated/trailing compressed data, and
bytes after IEND. Server tests prove rejection precedes provider calls and does
not change retained bytes or findings.

## Evidence and references

A temporary check on this laptop confirmed Node v24.22.1 exposes `crc32`, the
known CRC32 result for `123456789` is `cbf43926`, output over `maxOutputLength` is
rejected, and `info.engine.bytesWritten` detects trailing compressed input. This
verifies those building blocks, not the future complete PNG validator or browser
capture path.

Primary references: [PNG Third Edition](https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/) for the
format, and [Node v24.22.1 zlib documentation](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.22.1/doc/api/zlib.md)
for CRC and bounded inflation. The restricted admission policy and its limits
above are this project's explicit choices.

## DR-08 — actual browser gate and the 30-second measurement

### Qualifying inputs and required outcomes

Use the presentation laptop, the target Chromium browser, the local live server,
an actual microphone, and consenting adult role-play with original synthetic
work. Draw/write directly in the browser; do not inject a PNG, upload the
synthetic WAV, use a fake microphone, or preselect an expected result. Keep both
student and teacher views visibly in live mode. No fixture fallback is allowed.

A qualifying short sample has one completed continuous spoken explanation of
**5 through 20 seconds**, inclusive, measured from the recorder's actual start
to stop events, plus bounded freehand work and an authored regrouping assignment.
Recording and drawing are completed before the timed Submit action. All normal
60-second/10-MiB audio and PNG admission limits still apply. A longer/shorter
sample may be useful exploratory evidence but does not satisfy this timed gate.

Exercise these four prescribed cases through normal server-issued assignments:

| Case | Adult's submitted work/explanation | Required observed decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clear correct exchange | `27 + 18 = 45`; show and explain ten of fifteen ones becoming one ten, retaining five ones and all four tens | Usable supported exchange and its context-eligible authored next action; no claim of independent success if the assignment was assisted practice |
| Clear addition error | `27 + 18 = 35`; explicitly show/explain keeping five ones and dropping the ten | Supported `addition-omitted-ten` and reviewed addition teaching action |
| Clear subtraction error | `42 - 17 = 35`; explicitly show/explain four tens and twelve ones without reducing the tens | Supported `subtraction-value-changed` and reviewed subtraction teaching action |
| Ambiguous/conflicting evidence | Deliberately unclear marks or a visible exchange that contradicts the spoken account | Visible neutral clarification, with no disputed supported finding committed |

Use ordinary lesson operations to reach subtraction practice; any preceding
setup submissions remain labeled synthetic and are recorded separately. Do not
invent a target-selection endpoint, change an assignment's purpose, or inject a
judgment to reach the required case. Use separate learners or reset/rehearse as
needed to preserve the authored context. Record every gate attempt, not only the
fastest result. Transcript/image corrections and unexpected outcomes are part of
the record; an interpretation that changes a case's intended meaning fails its
case even if the UI responds quickly.

### Clock events and review-time accounting

Use one browser `performance.now()` time base for the following events and keep
their attempt ID, work/evidence version, and accepted snapshot revision together:

| Timestamp | Exact event |
| --- | --- |
| `t0` | The student's Submit handler begins, before PNG serialization, attempt admission, or audio upload; the completed recording and drawing are already ready |
| `tTranscriptReady` | The returned transcript is fully rendered and the confirm/edit controls are enabled |
| `tTranscriptConfirm` | The participant's confirm/correct handler begins, before its outgoing assessment request |
| `tImageReady` | The neutral image readback is fully rendered and its match/mismatch controls are enabled; candidate mathematical feedback remains withheld |
| `tImageConfirm` | The participant's match/mismatch handler begins, before its outgoing readback mutation |
| `tFinal` | The student view first renders the server-accepted reviewed teaching/next-step action or neutral `needs_clarification` decision for this current evidence version, with its committed snapshot revision |

`tFinal` cannot be a recording-stopped notice, upload success, transcription
screen, pending state, provisional assessment, or image readback screen. If the
participant rejects a readback, the final visible clarification must still come
from the accepted mismatch operation. If a live candidate needs clarification
without an image review, the final committed clarification is the end event and
there is no image-review pause to subtract.

Compute and report:

```text
wallMs = tFinal - t0
transcriptReviewMs = tTranscriptConfirm - tTranscriptReady
imageReviewMs = tImageConfirm - tImageReady              # only if reached
processingMs = wallMs - transcriptReviewMs - imageReviewMs
```

Only those explicit participant-review intervals are excluded from processing
time. Their full durations, including participant edits, are retained in wall
time. Keep serialization, upload, server work, both provider calls, request/poll
delay, rendering, and all request/correction submission overhead in
`processingMs`. Do not stop or pause the clock while a provider is working or
while an unexplained UI delay occurs. Missing/reordered timestamps invalidate a
measurement. A separate teaching/clarification turn after the displayed final
decision is a new cycle, not extra hidden review time in the measured cycle.

All three clear short cases must reach their required final decision with
`processingMs <= 30,000`. The ambiguous case must remain uncertain; record both
times for it as well. Report `processingMs`, `wallMs`, both participant-review
durations, actual recording duration, outcome/action, corrections, and any failed
attempt. The 45-second per-provider timeout remains a safety bound; it is not a
substitute for the 30-second demo criterion. This defines acceptance, not a
latency result or statistical performance claim.

After each final decision, observe the teacher's next successful scheduled
snapshot update and verify it contains the same accepted evidence/revision and
the corresponding counts or clarification flag. Record its observed update
delay separately from the student processing clock. Inspect the original drawing
and confirmed transcript in that view, and confirm there is no teacher audio
replay. A teacher display with canned/preseeded counts cannot satisfy this check.

Proceed with the full live demonstration only if the clear cases preserve their
intended meaning, the ambiguous case stays uncertain, recognition review exposes
no solution cue, the timing criterion passes, and teacher state derives from
those same accepted events. On capture/interpretation failure, simplify the
authored visual representation and rerun with a separately recorded result; if
it still fails, record the live multimodal path as unready and obtain an explicit
author decision for a fallback scope change. Passing synthetic audio or fixture
browser tests does not replace this gate. Passing this adult laptop gate also
does not establish child speech/drawing accuracy, classroom scale, learning
effectiveness, or retention.
